title: Perf pass: caching + request parallelization
description: From Tony (2026-07-29) while confirming word-based CursorHold re-fire. Candidates: (1) session cache of resolved class structures keyed on loc/model.hash — repeated opens of the same function or type currently re-chase everything; (2) parallelize the per-leaf hover fan-out (wuf) — ~8 sequential hovers contribute to the ~800ms uvicorn.run open, and coroutine-parallel requests are the obvious lever; (3) parsed-buffer reuse for typeshed-adjacent .py files; (4) measure CursorHold-mode request volume in real editing before optimizing it. Requirements doc already calls for 'cacheable by type-signature hash'.
close_reason: U2 complete, exit criteria beaten (uvicorn.run, real basedpyright, M1 Air): warm reopen 5-11ms (target <100ms) via resolve cache keyed on def-location + filetype + depth, invalidated by def-buffer changedtick, capped at 50 entries; cached trees preserve folds/lazy expansions/LLM values across reopens (feature, not accident) with active-param flags cleared per open. Cold open 412ms (target <500ms, was ~800ms): hover enrichment converted from ~8 sequential awaits to a single parallel fan-out (lsp.request_cb building block + counter-resume await); unannotated-param inference hovers joined the same fan-out; per-node informative-answer selection unchanged (all candidate refs fired concurrently, first informative wins in ref order). recurse() enriches its subtree the same way. First-ever open still ~900ms — that includes basedpyright's own initial file analysis, outside our control. e2e: cache-persistence + edit-invalidation cases (mock reads disk → buster must :write; real servers get didChange). Deferred: definition-chase parallelization (bigger refactor, not needed for targets).

title: Declaration fallback: retry textDocument/declaration when definition doesn't land on a def (getpass case)
description: basedpyright resolves stdlib names to runtime impl where the name may be a conditional assignment (getpass = unix_getpass). Retry with declaration → typeshed stub → annotated signature parses fine. Discovered by Tony testing shot_crud.py:137.
notes:
- Root cause: textDocument/definition is a RUNTIME question; basedpyright sends stdlib getpass to getpass.py where the name is a conditional assignment (getpass = unix_getpass), not a def
- Fix: when function_info finds no function_definition, retry once with textDocument/declaration (static universe → typeshed stub → annotated def, same parse path)
- Second fix from same session: typeshed guard extended to runtime stdlib (/lib/pythonX.Y/ minus site-packages) — TextIO's definition lands in runtime typing.py which contains no 'typeshed' in path
- Empty variant children (resolved class, zero fields+methods) no longer added
- Hygiene: extractor looked up by filetype not hardcoded 'python'; lazy hooks carry their impl ref
- Mock server now serves declaration (defs only) vs definition (alias assignments win) to mimic basedpyright; fixtures prompting.py/prompting_stub.py reproduce the getpass shape
- Verified against real basedpyright on shot_crud.py:137: renders prompt/stream/returns from stub

title: Cold-open prefetch (LspAttach kick + CursorHold cache warm) + ollama autostart tied to nvim lifetime
notes:
- Warmstart lives in init.lua setup(): LspAttach hover-at-(0,0) kick (plus a sweep of already-attached buffers — lazy ft loading races LspAttach), CursorHold prefetch, early ollama warmup
- Prefetch discards results; the cache write inside function_scope is the point. Guards: python ft, normal mode, no open session, buf:line:cword suppression key, single-flight token cancelled by M.open(). Skipped when trigger=hover. Config flag 'prefetch' default true
- ollama.autostart (default off, on in dotfiles): non-detached vim.system child is the real teardown guarantee — nvim kills it on ANY exit path; VimLeavePre SIGTERM is just graceful. ensure_server probes first and never touches a server it didn't spawn (verified live: manual server survived nvim exit)
- Chosen over brew services because of 8GB RAM: keep_alive holds ~2GB, so server lifetime = editor lifetime reclaims it on quit
- Warmup bug fixed: 'warmed' was set before the curl landed, permanently disabling retry if nvim started with the server down; now resets on failure
- Gotcha: init.lua closures must be defined AFTER 'local session' or they capture a global
- Test seam: resolve._cache_count(); suppression asserted by clearing cache and re-firing same-word CursorHold

POST-CLOSE REGRESSION (fixed same day): async.lua's global-generation staling meant ANY token mint staled all older tokens. Warmstart's LspAttach kicks fire for def-site buffers the pipeline itself loads → killed the running open/prefetch → K silently fell back to builtin hover; only reproducible with real lspconfig auto-attach (mock e2e has none). Fix: stale = cancelled only; explicit open_token supersession in M.open. Lesson: the one-pipeline-at-a-time assumption was load-bearing in async.token — concurrent pipelines need explicit ownership.

title: Hover-backed evaluated leaves for unresolvable/generic types
description: Where structural resolution gives up (unsolved TypeVar, unresolvable name), request hover at that position and render pyright's evaluated string as leaf text. Bounded per-leaf request cost; upgrades the 'raw annotation' fallback to evaluated truth.
notes:
- Trigger: node with refs but zero children after attach (alias/TypeVar/unresolvable, not _lazy) → hover refs in order (max 3), keep first INFORMATIVE answer — bare name echoes ('(class) Protocol' behind typeshed guard) decorate nothing, alias expansions do
- Unannotated params: hover the param NAME (function_info now records name_row/name_col) → pyright's inferred type; declared 'Any' suppressed in render, shows just '≈ int'
- Presentation: declared display stays primary, evaluated appended as style.evaluated marker (≈ unicode/rounded, ~ ascii/minimal) + text in TypeScopeEvaluated (links Comment); only when it differs from declared
- evaluated_from_hover lives in extract/python.lua — pyright's '(kind) name: T' hover shapes are language-server-specific, so parsing belongs to the language impl
- UNIFICATION DATAPOINT: uvicorn.run full open incl ~8 sequential hover enrichments = ~770ms with real basedpyright (cold-ish); parallelizing hovers is the obvious lever if an insert-mode surface needs faster
- Mock server hover now mimics pyright shapes (alias assignments → '(type alias) X: rhs', else '(parameter) x: int')
- gc0 (structural alias expansion) remains complementary: hover gives the STRING expansion, gc0 would give expandable CHILDREN
